question.text: If $(x+3)$ is a factor of $p(x) = 2x^3 + 5x^2 + kx - 3,$ then $k = $
question.explanation:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x - r)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ then the root $x = r$ is also a root of $p(x).$

Here, we are considering the factor $(x+3).$ The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to $0$ and solving: \begin{align} x + 3 & = 0\\ x & = -3 \end{align}

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+3)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ the root $x = -3$ is also a root of $p(x).$ This means $p \left( -3 \right) = 0,$ so we have \begin{align} 2(-3)^3 + 5(-3)^2 + k(-3) - 3 & = 0\\[3pt] -54 + 45 - 3k - 3 & = 0\\[3pt] -3k & = 12\\[3pt] k & = -4. \end{align}

question.explanation:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x - r)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ then the root $x = r$ is also a root of $p(x).$

Here, we are considering the factor $(x+1).$ The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to $0$ and solving: \begin{align} x + 1 & = 0\\ x & = -1 \end{align}

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+1)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ the root $x = -1$ is also a root of $p(x).$ This means $p \left( -1 \right) = 0,$ so we have \begin{align} p(-1) & = 0\\[3pt] 3(-1)^2 + a(-1) - 2 & = 0\\[3pt] 3 - a - 2 & = 0\\[3pt] a & = 1. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $(x-2)$ and $(3x-1)$ are factors of $f(x) = 3x^3 + ax^2 + bx + 2,$ then $a+b=$
question.explanation:
According to the factor theorem, if $(ax-b)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x = \dfrac{b}{a}$ is also a root of $f(x).$

Here, we are considering the factors $(x-2)$ and $(3x-1).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

\begin{align} x-2 = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= 2 \\ 3x-1 = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= \dfrac{1}{3} \end{align}

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x-2)$ and $(3x-1)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=2$ and $x=\dfrac{1}{3}$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(2)=0$ and $f\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 0,$ so we have \begin{align} f(2) & = 0\\[5pt] 3(2)^3 + a(2)^2 + b(2) + 2 & = 0\\[5pt] 24 + 4a + 2b + 2 & = 0\\[5pt] 4a + 2b & = -26\\[5pt] 2a + b & = -13,\\ \\ f\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) & = 0\\[5pt] 3\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^3 + a\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 + b\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + 2 & = 0\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{a}{9} + \dfrac{b}{3} + 2 & = 0\\[5pt] 1 + a + 3b + 18 & = 0\\[5pt] a + 3b & = -19\\[5pt] -2a - 6b & = 38. \end{align}

This gives a system of equations \[ \begin{cases} 2a + b = -13 \\[3pt] -2a - 6b = 38. \end{cases} \]

Adding the equations, we eliminate $a$ and get \[ -5b = 25\quad\Rightarrow\quad b=-5. \]

Substituting $b=-5$ in either equation gives $a=-4.$ So our solutions are $a=-4$ and $b=-5.$ Finally then,

\[ a+b = -4 + (-5) = -9. \]

example.title: Finding Two Unknown Coefficients of a Polynomial Given Two Factors

question.text: Given that $x$ and $(x+4)$ are factors of $f(x)=ax^3+11x^2-4x+b,$ determine $a + b.$
question.explanation:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x = r$ is also a root of $f(x).$

Here, we are considering the factors $x$ and $(x+4).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

\begin{align} x = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= 0 \\ x+4 = 0 &\quad \Rightarrow \quad x= -4 \end{align}

According to the factor theorem, then, since $x$ and $(x+4)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=0$ and $x=-4$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(0) = 0$ and $f(-4)=0,$ so we have \begin{align} f(0) & = 0\\[3pt] a(0)^3 + 11(0)^2 - 4(0) + b & = 0\\[3pt] b & = 0, \\ \\ f(-4) & = 0\\[3pt] a(-4)^3 + 11(-4)^2 - 4(-4) + b & = 0\\[3pt] -64a + 176 + 16 + b & = 0\\[3pt] -64a + 192 + 0 & = 0\\[3pt] -64a & = -192\\[3pt] a & = 3. \end{align}

So our solutions are $a=3$ and $b=0.$ Finally then, \[ a+b = 3+0 = 3. \]
